title: Plan first: add pagination to a small API
goal: Add ?page and ?limit pagination to GET /items without breaking existing clients. Get a written plan out of the agent, critique and edit it, commit PLAN.md, and only then let the agent write code.
setup_cmd: cp -r exercises/ex-3-1-plan-first/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-3-1-plan-first && cd ~/fm-ex/ex-3-1-plan-first && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm starter

starter_prompts.claude: Start in plan mode (Shift+Tab, or /plan). Prompt: "Add pagination to GET /items. Read src/app.js and everything in tests/ first (tests/pagination.test.js is the spec; do not edit it). Produce a plan with these sections: Goal (and out of scope), Files to change, Steps, Risks and open questions (especially anything that breaks existing callers or handles invalid input), Verification. Ask me before assuming anything." Critique the plan, press Ctrl+G to edit it, then approve with manual edit approval and say: "Save the approved plan to PLAN.md and stop. Write no code."
starter_prompts.codex: In a read-only session (codex -s read-only) run: /plan Add pagination to GET /items. Read src/app.js and everything in tests/ first (tests/pagination.test.js is the spec; do not edit it). Produce a plan with these sections: Goal (and out of scope), Files to change, Steps, Risks and open questions (especially anything that breaks existing callers or handles invalid input), Verification. Ask me before assuming anything. Critique the plan in chat, then say: "Save the approved plan to PLAN.md. Write no code." (Or capture it in one shot with codex exec "<same prompt>" | tee PLAN.md.)

solution_notes: The plan is written before any code, and it names src/app.js as the only production file to change, so the diff can be checked against it.

It makes the backwards-compatibility decision explicit: the body stays a bare array, totals go in headers, and pagination only switches on when limit is sent. Changing the body shape would have broken every existing client.
Invalid input is specified in advance (400 with an error for bad or oversized limit and page, and for page without limit), and a page past the end returns an empty array.
Verification is concrete: the exact command, plus a manual curl check that the no-query response is unchanged.
